ActorDisplayModeSwap:
Utility JSL (Bank 06) that actor init code calls first: it saves the actor's variant index and then puts the actor on the normal visible run path.

Effects, with the actor's own DP as D (the caller is an actor script, D = X = slot):
  $24 = low nibble of $0E (the OAM attribute XOR word; for a scene-data actor with an odd spawn byte 2 the word is byte 2 >> 1, so the nibble is the variant index chosen in the scene's actor list). Callers read it back later, e.g. wa78_water_kid's interact handler feeds $24 to SwitchCase.
  $0E = $2000 (attribute high byte $20 = sprite priority 2).
  $10 (actor flags 1): bit $2000 cleared (hidden in sprite composition / script-driven run path) and bit $1000 set (display-active: processed when displayModeFlags bit 7 filters the actor list).

Of the 25 actor-def headers in the 22 caller files, 24 start with flags word $1000 or $1800 (bit $2000 already clear, $1000 already set), so for them the $10 update changes nothing and the effective work is $0E = $2000 plus the $24 save. Only eu91_shop_queue starts with $3000, where the $2000 clear is real.

The $0E written here is the actor's own attribute word, not the global displayModeFlags ($09EC).

Requires M = 0 (16-bit A). Call sites: 23 in 22 NPC actor files: watermia (wa78_women, water_kid, moving_woman, men, children, centipede_man), angel_village (av6B_villagers1-3, ocean_ache, av6C_villagers4-5, av69_signs), seaside_palace (sp5A_villagers), euro (eu91_women1-2, men1-2, shop_queue, merchant twice, eu9D_slaves) and dao sweatshop (daC5_weaver).
av69_erik:
Erik at the Angel Village entrance — ambient party member.

NPC at the tunnel entrance. No direct dialog in initial
state — positioned as part of the party formation entering
the village.
av69_kara:
Kara at the Angel Village entrance — excited and teasing.

NPC. Says: "What! Will! Come with me! What are you grinning
about?" Playful dialog as the party arrives at the village.
av69_lance:
Controller of the arrival cutscene at the Angel Village entrance (scene $69); the actor prints Neil's and Lance's lines.

The actor dies at spawn when flag $8D (the Watermia arrival has started) or flag $75 (this cutscene was shown) is set. Otherwise it locks the joypad ($CFFC), prints 'Neil: We're here at last...' and 'Lance: Look! A sign!', walks, prints the sign discussion, and sets scratch flag $01 (Lilly, Neil and Erik walk). It then waits for scratch $04 (the end of the Lilly/Kara exchange), sets persistent flag $75, walks to its final position and unlocks the joypad.

The chain of scratch flags is $01 Lance, $02 Lilly, $03 Kara, $04 Lilly; the other four av69 actors run the same two death tests.
av69_lily:
Lilly at the Angel Village entrance — urges the party forward.

NPC. Lilly: "Will, let's go." Brief encouragement to
explore the village.
av69_neil:
Neil at the Angel Village entrance — ambient party member.

NPC at the entrance. Positioned as part of the arriving
party formation.
av69_signs:
Welcome signs at the Angel Village entrance.

Readable sign objects. Text: "Travellers, Please use this room.
Angel Tribe." Establishes the village's hospitality.
av6A_erik:
Erik in the Angel Village annex (scene $6A); he runs the reunion cutscene after Kara's rescue.

At spawn: flag $8D set -> dies. Flag $A9 (reunion done) set -> code_06C513: placed at tile (16,0C) with the handler 'I think I saw a Red Jewel in the Angel Village.'. Flag $8C (Kara rescued) set -> code_06C4D7: locks the joypad ($CFFC), walks to tile (0F,0C) and on, prints the reunion dialog (Neil, Lilly and Kara react to Kara's return), sets flag $A9 and unlocks. Otherwise: installs the 'The sun is really bright. I never noticed that before.' handler.
av6A_kara:
Kara in the Angel Village annex — compares to a floating city.

NPC. Says: "In the Floating City, many houses are built
on rafts. Kind of like Watermia." Draws connections between
the locations the party has visited.
av6A_lance:
Lance in the Angel Village annex — confides something important.

Extended NPC (~104 lines). Says: "Will. I want to talk to you
about something. It's hard to say..." Part of the emotional
subplot about Lance's growing feelings and his necklace.
av6A_lily:
Lilly in the Angel Village annex — questions the dark environment.

NPC. Lilly: "Why do angels live in such a dark place? Feels
so gloomy." Provides atmosphere commentary about the
underground village.
av6A_neil:
Neil in the Angel Village annex (scene $6A); he offers the trip to Watermia once the party is reunited.

At spawn: flag $8D set -> dies. Flag $A9 (reunion done) set -> code_06C065: placed at tile (17,0E) in frame #15 with the handler code_06C077. Flag $8C (Kara rescued) set and $A9 clear -> code_06C056: starts at tile (0F,0E), walks four steps and falls into code_06C065. Otherwise: installs the 'I think the Angels are descendants of the Mu people.' handler.

code_06C077 asks 'Can we go now? Yes / Wait a minute'. Yes (row 1) prints 'I think it's very hot in the Floating City...', stages world-map move route #11 and queues scene $78 (Watermia) at (0250,0370); the other answers print 'There's no hurry. Take your time.'
av6B_door:
Door of the Angel Village (scene $6B).

At spawn the actor writes $0F into four bytes of the collision tile map ($7FC568, $7FC56A, $7FCA52, $7FCA54), nudges itself by (8,0) and installs an interact handler. If the player is near (BranchIfPlayerNear #01) it opens at once; otherwise it waits for scratch flag $01, which the interact handler sets.

Opening plays sound #06 on channel 2, applies BgChange #45 and writes the shared phase word $0AA6 := 0 (the counter that the undersea-tunnel actors and the test scene read). The actor never closes the door and no persistent flag records it: every load of scene $6B starts with the door closed unless the player spawns next to it.
av6B_flame:
Torch flame in Angel Village — animated fire decoration.

Looping flame sprite on a wall sconce. Provides ambient
lighting in the dim underground village.
av6B_musician:
Harp-playing woman in Angel Village — dialog about music.

NPC: "Music is the best medicine for the soul. The right
sound can heal any wound." Reflects the Angel Tribe's
belief in music's spiritual power.
av6B_ocean_ache:
Villager longing for the ocean in Angel Village.

NPC: "I don't know when we started living here. But when
I look at the ocean, I feel an ache..." Expresses the
Angel Tribe's yearning for the surface world they left.
av6B_villagers1:
Angel villager group 1 — introduces the village and sun weakness.

Extended NPC (~111 lines). "This is the Angel Village.
If our bodies are exposed to the sun for long..." Explains
the Angel Tribe's vulnerability to sunlight and why they
live underground.
av6B_villagers2:
Angel villager group 2 — emotionless existence.

NPC: "We have no emotions... I've neither laughed nor cried
since the day I was born." Reveals the Angel Tribe's
emotional numbness — a key theme of their devolution.
av6B_villagers3:
Angel villager group 3 — evolution theory.

NPC: "It's been said that we are the form into which humans
evolve." Presents the Angel Tribe as humanity's potential
future — or a warning about devolution.
av6C_harpist:
Harpist NPC in the Angel Village rooms — ambient musician.

Decorative NPC playing a harp with looping animation.
No interaction dialog. Provides atmosphere for the
village's musical culture.
av6C_only_sleeping:
Sleeping angel villager — Will's observation.

Interactable NPC. Will remarks: "She appears to be sleeping.
It's like the spirit's drawn out..." Hints at the Angel
Tribe's declining vitality and connection to the comet.
av6C_portrait:
Portrait interactive object in the Angel Village rooms.

Examinable painting on the wall. When interacted with,
may reveal hidden content or provide visual detail about
the Angel Tribe's history.
av6C_villagers4:
Angel villager group 4 — dance culture NPC.

NPC who says: "People here love to dance." Part of the
village's cultural exposition, showing how the Angel Tribe
preserves their identity through art.
av6C_villagers5:
Angel villager group 5 — dancing to feel human.

NPC: "I dance to remember what it feels like to be human.
But..." Melancholy reflection on the Angel Tribe's lost
humanity. Ties into the game's evolution/devolution theme.
av6D_flame_left:
Left-side flame decoration in the Angel Village tunnels.

Static torch sprite on the left wall. Ambient lighting
for the tunnel corridors.
av6D_flame_right:
Right-side flame decoration in the Angel Village tunnels.

Static torch sprite on the right wall. Paired with
flame_left for symmetrical corridor lighting.
av70_crawlspace:
Crawlspace passage in the Angel Village river tunnel.

Interactive passageway with size check. Text: "The entrance
is too small!" Blocks passage for Will's normal form —
requires a smaller form (Shadow) to pass through.
av70_flame_center:
Center flame decoration in the Angel Village river tunnel.

Animated torch sprite in the center of a tunnel room.
Ambient visual element.
av70_hidden_passage:
Hidden passage discovery in the Angel Village river tunnel.

Interactable wall crack: "The wind blows through a crack
in the wall. I found a hidden passage!" Reveals a secret
path to a treasure or alternate route.
av71_wind_effect:
Wind visual effect in the Angel Village wind tunnel.

Animated wind particle effect. Creates visible air currents
that blow through the tunnel passage. Indicates direction
and strength of the wind.
av73_waterfall_sound:
Waterfall sound and alcove flag in the waterfall tunnel (scene $73).

At spawn, if the player is inside tiles (00,00)-(40,10) the actor sets scratch flag $00 and dies. Otherwise it spawns a watcher (code_06D733) that sets scratch $00 while the player is inside tiles (2A,17)-(2F,1D) and clears it everywhere else, and its main script writes APUIO0 = $40 + min(2 * |playerXTile - $2C|, $30) every fourth frame, so the value grows with the horizontal distance from tile column $2C. What the sound engine does with that port value (volume or another parameter) is not traced here.

Scratch $00 is read by the player's idle, ladder and shimmy code, which selects the alternate sprite set while it is set.
av74_ishtar:
Ishtar and her self-portrait in the tunnel rooms (scene $74).

Flag $89 is set by the test scene ($75) after the fourth correct answer. With $89 clear the actor stands at its post in frame #12 and its interact handler prints 'I wonder if you're here to get Kara. Go into this room. If you solve all the riddles, I'll give back the girl.'; with $89 set the actor dies at spawn.

At spawn the actor also starts a child actor (code_06CEB8, offset (0,-16)) for the self-portrait. With $89 clear the child shows frame #13 and has no interact handler. With $89 set it shows frame #15 and installs the handler code_06CEDF, which sets flag $8B and prints the long speech ('I have been waiting for you. Sprinkle magic powder on the painting, and give it a kiss...') the first time and '.............' on every later talk.

No actor of scene $74 starts a fight (the scene lists the player, the camera, av74_kara, av74_ishtar and a hidden Red Jewel).
av74_kara:
Kara's picture and the rescue cutscene in the tunnel rooms (scene $74).

The actor dies at spawn when flag $8C (Kara rescued) is set. Otherwise it spawns a child (code_06D251, offset (0,16)) that carries the picture's interact handler, and polls BranchIfHasItem #14 (Magic Dust); only while the player carries the item does it enter code_06D171.

The picture's handler (code_06D25A): with flag $89 (Ishtar's test passed) clear it prints 'Kara's picture. She is contained inside it....'. With $89 set and scratch flag $01 clear it prints 'If I don't spread magic dust...'. With $89 set and scratch flag $01 set it prints the kiss text and sets flag $8A. Scratch $01 is set by UseItem_MagicPowder when the player uses the Magic Dust in tiles (07,08)-(09,0A) of this scene, and is cleared by every scene load.

code_06D171 waits for scratch $01 and then flag $8A, locks the joypad ($FFFC), fades the backdrop out twice, loads the Nazca sprite set and runs the rescue: Kara walks up, three dialogs between Kara and Will (they start with Kara's 'Will....Sorry for being so selfish.'), then it sets flag $8C and queues scene $6A (the Angel Village annex).
av75_apprentice:
Ishtar's apprentice in the test scene ($75).

At spawn the actor tests the player against tiles (70,00)-(80,10), the last observation room. Inside, it sets scratch flag $00 (the byte the player code reads to select the alternate idle sprite set) and writes playerSpeedNs := $FFFF. It then places itself by $0AA6 >> 1: 1 -> tile (3A,1D), 2 -> (57,1D), 3 -> (00,71); other values keep the placed position.

The actor marks itself solid and its interact handler prints 'When you solve the puzzle of the room you may pass.'
av75_voice_doors:
Door objects of Ishtar's test corridor (scene $75): eight actors share this script, the door index 0-7 being the low nibble of the actor word $0E.

An actor dies at spawn when flag $89 (test passed) is set or when the player is inside a room (Y < $F0). In the corridor it installs an interact handler that compares the phase word $0AA6 with the door index: a smaller counter prints 'Ishtar's voice resounds. Don't hurry. Open the doors in order from the left.', a larger one prints 'That door is already open. There's no need to open it.', an equal one plays sound #0E, applies BgChange #49 + index and sets word flag $0149 + index.
av75_voice_rooms:
Room controller of Ishtar's test (scene $75), one actor.

The actor dies at spawn when the player is in the corridor (Y >= $F0). In a room it first clears the eight door flags $0149-$0150. A view room (playerXTile bit 4 clear) increments the phase word $0AA6, locks the joypad ($CFFC), prints 'Learn well the condition of that room...' and unlocks.

An answer room (bit 4 set) locks the joypad, prints 'Show how it's different from the room before.', spawns a cursor actor (code_06DBF3, moved by the D-pad) at the player position and waits for the button press (BranchIfPressed #$8001). playerXTile >> 5 selects room 0-3 and its cursor box. Inside the box it prints that room's 'Right answer!' text and increments $0AA6; in room 3 it instead sets flag $89 and word flag $0151 (test passed). Outside the box it prints 'How are your powers of observation?... Try again!!' and decrements $0AA6. The actor then unlocks the joypad and dies.
mu60_floor_spikes:
Floor spike trap in Mu — timed hazard on the floor.

Environmental trap that extends spikes at timed intervals.
Damages the player on contact during the extended phase.
Uses a simple timer loop for the extend/retract cycle.
mu60_force_ball:
Force Ball hazard — bouncing energy projectile in Mu.

Moving hazard that bounces off walls in a predictable pattern.
Damages the player on contact. Uses velocity vectors with
wall collision reversal for the bounce physics. Spawned
by room setup and persists until the player leaves.
mu61_hint:
Lilly's hint in Mu south — thinking about the dungeon.

Lilly speaks from Will's pocket: "Will. I've been thinking..."
Provides a gameplay hint for navigating the Mu dungeon.
Uses the "speaks from pocket" framing for spirit companion.
mu62_hope_statue:
Statue of Hope pickups of the Mu west room (scene $62) and the Mu maze (scene $65).

mu62_hope_statue sets flag $78 as soon as it spawns, installs an interact handler and dies once flag $79 is set. The handler does nothing while music is playing; otherwise it calls GiveItem #12 (Statue of Hope), sets $79 and shows "You've found the Statue of Hope! ... Was there a room with the same name...?". A full inventory prints the inventory-is-full message and leaves $79 clear. mu62_hope_statue2 (the maze) does the same with flag $7F and the text "Was there another room with the same name...?".

The statue is a key item: UseItem_StatueOfHope consumes it on a pedestal of the prayer room (scene $63). It gives no stat boost.
mu63_spirits:
Statue of Hope pedestal show in the Mu prayer room (scene $63).

A player standing inside tiles (10,00)-(20,10) when the actor spawns selects the east branch (flag $7E, pedestal at pixel (0180,0058)); otherwise the west branch runs (flag $7B, pedestal at (0080,0058)). With the branch's flag already set the actor only spawns the placed-statue sprite and dies. Otherwise it waits for UseItem_StatueOfHope to set the flag, spawns the sprite, locks the joypad ($CFFC), plays music #1B, fades the backdrop in and spawns ten helper sprites (six of code_069C14, four of code_069BDA). It then prints the single text "The Sun god... Rama... The ocean holds a power...", sets scratch $02 so that every helper sprite leaves, fades the backdrop out, unlocks the joypad and dies.
mu64_switch_spikes:
Switch-activated spike trap in the Mu connector area.

Floor spikes that toggle state when a switch is hit. Unlike
timed floor_spikes, these respond to puzzle switches.
Used in the connector passages between Mu rooms.
mu66_altar_dialog:
Altar room dialog — describes the ancient burial ground of Mu.

Text object: "This looks like an ancient burial ground for
the people of Mu." Provides context about the altar room's
significance as a sacred space for the ancient Mu civilization.
mu66_altar1:
Statue sprite and scene reload of the first altar in the Mu altar room (scene $66).

Waits for flag $80 (Rama Statue placed on the first pedestal by UseItem_RamaStatue), shows its statue frame #2D and waits for $81. When both flags are set and the player stands outside tiles (00,00)-(20,20) it locks the joypad ($CFFC), waits #1D ticks and queues a map change to scene $66 at pixel (00F8,01D8). It sets no flag.
mu66_altar2:
Statue sprite of the second altar in the Mu altar room (scene $66).

Waits for flag $81 (Rama Statue placed on the second pedestal by UseItem_RamaStatue), then shows its statue frame #2D and idles. It sets no flag.
mu66_rama_spirits:
King Rama's spirit council — major exposition scene in Mu (~199 lines).

Rama introduces himself: "I am Rama, King of Mu. My body
passed on long ago, but my spirit lives on." Then: "Hear
the words of spirits awakened." Extended multi-spirit dialog
revealing the history of Mu, the ocean's power, and hints
about the comet. Key lore dump for the Mu chapter.
mu67_bomb:
Bomb of the Mu vampire lair (scene $67) — a two-wire question and a countdown.

The bomb stands solid next to Erik. Its interact handler asks "There's a red wire and a blue wire sticking out of the bomb... Cut which one?"; either answer prints "The red wire is cut!" or "The blue wire is cut!" and sets scratch $01, so the choice has no consequence. Once enemiesRemaining is 0 the main script changes the player back to Will if needed, applies BG changes #46 and #47 and sets $0146 and $0147; then it waits for $01. After the wire is cut it locks the joypad, plays music #1B and sound #2C, prints "Will: The bomb has been defused..." with Erik's and Lilly's lines, sets scratch $03 (Neil's cue), applies BG change #93, unlocks the joypad and dies.

A second actor spawned at the start is the countdown. It waits for scratch $02 (the fight has started), counts down from BCD $0140 by one per #3C ticks (paused while displayModeFlags bit $2000 is set), shows the digits with ComposeDigitSprites and dies when $01 is set. If the count passes zero while a vampire is alive, playerHp is set to 0; with both vampires dead it prints "It was a dud. I'm saved...".
mu67_erik:
Erik trapped in the vampire lair — screaming for help.

Multi-state NPC: before rescue, Erik shouts: "Heeeeelp!!
Someone save me!!" During the bomb sequence: "First, defuse
the bomb! Hurry! Hurry!" Part of the climactic rescue in
the vampire lair.
mu67_kara:
Kara in the vampire lair — pragmatic about escaping.

Says: "It doesn't matter! Let's think about how to leave Mu!"
Focused on survival rather than the drama. Brief NPC
during the vampire lair escape.
mu67_lair_curtain:
Curtain decoration in the vampire lair entrance.

Visual prop that reveals the lair behind it. No dialog.
Animated curtain sprite for atmosphere.
mu67_neil_lily:
Neil and Lilly in the vampire lair — reunion after the battle.

Two-character NPC (~95 lines). Neil: "Will! Are you OK?!"
Lance: "Will! I don't see Lilly." Lilly reassures: "Sorry
I worried you. Will was protecting me, so I was OK."
Multi-speaker dialog sequence after the vampire defeat.
sp58_descent_cutscene:
Descent cutscene — the party escapes the falling Sky Garden.

Scripted sequence where Neil's airplane attempts to catch
the falling party. Manages character sprite movement,
camera control, and the transition to the ocean scenes.
Leads into the Mu chapter.
sp58_missed_flight:
Neil's failed catch — comic relief during the descent.

Neil: "Shoot!! I dropped a contact!!" Kara: "You what!!!"
Brief comedic interlude during the tense descent sequence
where Neil fumbles the rescue attempt.
sp58_monologue:
Will's monologue after escaping the Sky Garden.

Narration: "We got out of the airplane in the nick of time...
Neil's amazing." Reflective text as the party leaves the
Sky Garden chapter behind. Locks joypad during playback.
sp58_red_eye:
Red Eye event — Neil comments on the close call and heads to Mu.

Multi-dialog NPC. Neil: "That was a close one!" Kara cries.
Then Neil suggests: "Well, to the ocean! Mu lies somewhere
in this ocean." Transitions the story toward the Mu chapter.
sp5A_monologue:
Will's monologue arriving at the Seaside Palace.

Narration: "The next thing he knew, Will was standing in a
huge palace." Will: "I couldn't remember anything..." Also
references Lilly and Mu. Sets the disorienting atmosphere
of the vampire palace.
sp5A_phantom_ribber:
Phantom Ribber in the Seaside Palace — harmless ghost.

Ghost NPC. Will: "That's odd. Even if I touch it no damage
occurs..." A phantom version of the Edward Castle enemy
that is intangible. Establishes the palace's supernatural
nature where normal threats don't apply.
sp5A_villagers:
Rescued villagers in the Seaside Palace — freed from demon form.

Multi-NPC group (~184 lines). "Saved!! Thank you!! I was
brought to this palace from Freejia and changed to a demon..."
Lilly helps translate. The villagers were transformed by
the vampire's fountain. Connects to the Freejia slave trade.
sp5A_voice:
Strange voice and room hints of the Seaside Palace (scene $5A).

While flag $70 is clear it checks five trigger boxes each frame; each box prints its text once and sets its latch. (37,28)-(38,29) with $71: "Strange Voice: This is the Palace of Vampires... The fountain in this palace produces demons continuously...". (0E,38)-(0F,39) with $72: "In the basement of the castle is a strange fountain. The stone is there... Hurry! Hurry!". (2B,59)-(2C,5A) with $73: "The Purification Stone... in the castle...". (36,07)-(3B,0B) with $83: "Will: What? A sign of life from the right-hand room...". (08,18)-(0B,1A) with $84: the same remark for the left-hand room.
sp5B_erik:
Erik trapped in the palace rooms — frightened in darkness.

NPC: "What is this place? Dark and lonely. Mother, save me..."
Erik's vulnerability in the palace. Each party member is
separated and trapped in different rooms.
sp5B_kara:
Kara trapped in the palace rooms — lost and confused.

NPC: "Will... Where... Where is it...??" Kara can't find
her way in the dark palace. Part of the separated party.
sp5B_lance:
Lance trapped in the palace rooms — unconscious groaning.

NPC: "Uhhhn. Uhhhn." Lance is barely conscious in his
room. Minimal dialog showing his weakened state.
sp5B_lily:
Lilly in the palace rooms — startled then relieved.

NPC (~72 lines). "Waaah!!" Lilly is scared. Then: "Hey...
You scared me!! I practically had a heart attack!!"
Lilly's relief at seeing Will. Comic moment in the
otherwise tense palace.
sp5B_neil:
Neil trapped in the palace rooms — unconscious groaning.

NPC: "Uhhhn. Uhhhn." Neil is barely conscious like Lance.
The party members are all weakened by the palace.
sp5C_key_coffin:
Key coffin of the Seaside Palace (scene $5C) — Lilly looks inside; no item is given.

Dies at spawn when word flag $013A is set. Otherwise it installs an interact handler and waits for scratch $01. The handler prints "Will: The coffins are lined up..." while flag $6F is clear; with $6F set it prints "Will: I can't seem to open the lid... Lilly: Wait a minute. Isn't there a hole in the coffin?..." and sets $01. The main script then locks the joypad ($CFFC), moves a sprite (frame #33 of spriteset_pickups_effects) from the player to the coffin, applies BG change #3A, sets $013A, prints "Lilly: Strange... There's a key fastened inside this coffin. No wonder it didn't open.", moves the sprite back to the player, unlocks the joypad and dies.
sp5C_stone_coffin:
Stone coffin of the Seaside Palace (scene $5C) — Lilly finds the Purification Stone (~151 lines).

Dies at spawn when word flag $013B is set. The interact handler prints "Will: The coffins are lined up..." while flag $6F is clear; with $6F set it prints the "Isn't there a hole in the coffin?" dialog and sets scratch $02. The main script then locks the joypad ($CFFC), moves a sprite (frame #33 of spriteset_pickups_effects) from the player to the coffin, applies BG change #3B, sets $013B and calls GiveItem #11 (Purification Stone): Lilly says "I found a strange stone inside this coffin." and "You've found the Purification Stone!" is shown. When GiveItem fails (inventory full) the script prints "...But your inventory is full..."; when it fails or music is playing it clears $013B and $02, moves the sprite back and waits for the next talk.
sp5D_fountain:
Demon fountain of the Seaside Palace (scene $5D) — the Purification Stone cutscene (~112 lines).

Dies at spawn when flag $70 is set, when $6F is clear or when the player does not hold item #11 (Purification Stone). Otherwise it locks the joypad, prints "Lilly: What!! It's a strange fountain... Could there be a connection between this and the rock...?", unlocks and waits for scratch $0E, which UseItem_PurificationStone sets inside tiles (0A,11)-(17,1A). It then locks the joypad ($EFFC), plays sound #25, moves its sprite from the player toward pixel (0100,0160), fades the backdrop out (scratch $0F is set while this runs), sets $70 (fountain purified), clears the fountain's solid tile (0D,0F) and unlocks the joypad.
sp5E_passageway:
Passageway discovery in the Seaside Palace.

Lilly speaks from pocket: "A passageway... I wonder if it
goes clear to Mu?" Reveals a connection between the
palace and Mu. Links the two underwater locations.
st68_ambient_bubbles:
Ambient bubble effect in the undersea tunnel.

Visual actor (~105 lines) that spawns floating bubble
sprites at random positions. Creates the underwater
atmosphere for the long tunnel passage. Uses RngByte
for random bubble placement.
st68_campfire:
Campfire in the undersea tunnel — rest stop decoration.

Animated campfire sprite at a rest area in the tunnel.
Provides visual warmth and marks a safe zone.
st68_erik:
Erik in the undersea tunnel (scene $68). The phase word $0AA6 selects the piece (SwitchCase 0, 1, 2).

Phase 0: waits for scratch flag $01 (Neil's narration done), walks to his camp position, installs the 'Hey, don't look!' handler and waits for scratch $04 (Kara's remark done). He then walks off, prints 'In this way, another day passed slowly...', increments $0AA6 and queues scene $68 again at (0070,01A0), which starts phase 1.

Phase 1: dies. Phase 2: placed at tile (17,1A) with no further behaviour.
st68_kara:
